+# Tc Differential Dispatcher
+
+Scripted CI dispatcher for parked differential rerun requests (TC-failure attribution, gh-1329 follow-up). A pure local-execution job — no AI CLI, the run is the verdict.
+
+When a validated guard TC fails and the automation leg's evidence cannot attribute the failure, the bug parks a differential rerun request in the TC maintenance ledger and carries the `tc_differential_pending` label (the SM rule queries it). This job — dispatched on the next SM tick, before any TC generator re-dispatches the bug — settles the request mechanically:
+
+1. **Run** — checkout the request's recorded last-green build (`lastGreenSha`) in the target repo and run the single TC script. Nothing but the build varies.
+2. **Route** — green on the old build → the change range caused the failure: the bug earns its bounce (moved to Ready For Development, evidence named in the comment). Red on the old build → the failure predates the change: the finding reopens as maintenance-debt sweep work. The bounce cap reached → owner escalation. A sibling-guard request never bounces its own bug.
+3. **Resolve** — post the updated ledger marker (the consumed parked section disappears), post the route report, and clear the park label when nothing remains parked.
+
+Unrunnable requests (no checkout target, no run command configured) stay parked fail-safe: one explanation comment on first attempt, quiet bumps afterwards, and the request remains visible in every ledger digest — an attribution stall is never silent.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `tcRunCommand` (customParams) — the single-TC command template with a `{testPath}` placeholder (e.g. `pytest {testPath}`). Required for any request to run; without it all requests stay parked with an explanation comment.
+- `workingDir` (customParams) — the target-repo checkout the TC scripts and git commands run in (default: project config `workingDir`).
+- `maxReworkRounds` (customParams) — the earned-bounce cap before owner escalation (default: the triage engine's default).
+- `parkLabel` (customParams) — the SM-matching park label (default `tc_differential_pending`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = tc_differential_pending`) must be overridden to match.
+
+The corresponding SM rule lives in `sm.json` (`Parked differential rerun requests → scripted CI dispatch`): it matches bugs carrying the park label, stamps its own `sm_tc_differential_triggered` crash-recovery label, and runs before the bug TC-generator rule so a parked bug is settled before a fresh generation dispatch (the generator rule also skips `tc_differential_pending` bugs).

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Duplication gate (gh-1251): a second, independent gate fails PRs and main on
# NEW or GROWING JS duplication. The measurement is
# `crap4js duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci`; a
# pinned set of production files already exceeds 1% today (pre-existing debt
# owned by the gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets — see duplication-baseline.json
# for the current pinned set), so the gate is a RATCHET against that
# baseline, not an absolute bar — it fails only when a file over threshold is
# not pinned or a pinned file gained ABSOLUTE duplicated lines
# (ci/duplicationRatchet.js; percentage shifts from file shrinkage are
# informational, not failures). Its clones-mode report also feeds the README
# `duplication` endpoint badge published from the same run.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |

arguments.command: sed -n '120,200p' .github/workflows/quality.yml

run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          node ci/duplicationRatchet.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" duplication-baseline.json "$code"

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e

content.thinking:
The transitive following is a pinned behavior (gh-961, with tests). So I can't just remove it. The over-collection happens because the transitive scan follows *framework plumbing* modules (configLoader.js → config.js, common/trackers.js, etc.) that read generic `customParams.*` from the object the action passes through.

The key insight for a principled fix: the transitive collection is meant for **action-specific helper modules** (extractions next to the action). Generic framework modules (configLoader, config, common/trackers, etc.) are consumed by nearly every agent and their customParams reads describe the FRAMEWORK, not the action. But where's the line? A simple, defensible rule: **transitive collection follows only requires that resolve to files in the same directory as the action** (`js/` siblings — gh-961's "helper modules next to the action"), not into `js/common/` subdirectories and not framework modules like `js/configLoader.js`/`js/config.js` at the js root... wait, the action IS in js/, so configLoader.js IS a sibling.

Hmm. Let me think about what actually distinguishes the noise. The reviewer says the dispatcher "reads exactly four: tcRunCommand, workingDir, maxReworkRounds, parkLabel" — the ones read directly in the action source. The transitive ones from configLoader/trackers are generic plumbing.

Option: keep transitive following but exclude reads that come from **generic plumbing modules consumed via a passed-through customParams object**: too semantic for a regex-based generator.

Alternative pragmatic approach used elsewhere in the repo? gh-1247 added `collectDelegatedCommonBodies` precisely to avoid "importing every literal in the helper module (over-reporting)" — for artifacts/side-effects they scan ONLY the delegated method bodies. But paramsUsed still uses `collectCustomParamsUsageFrom` which follows whole modules.

Hmm wait — actually, is it truly whole-module? `collectCustomParamsUsageFrom(filePath, src, visited)` follows local requires of the action itself recursively. For the dispatcher: requires configLoader.js → configLoader requires config.js? and others; trackers.js requires config.js, ticketKeyShapes... The union of `customParams\.` matches in that closure = the 15.

What's the minimal, principled change that fixes the dispatcher doc (and docs generally) without breaking the gh-961 pinned tests? The gh-961 tests use *sibling helper modules* (`doThingHelpers.js`, `mid.js`, `leaf.js`) — plain files next to the action. A rule "follow local relative requires only while they stay within the action's own directory" would break nothing in those tests (all in agents/js/), but for real actions in `js/`, configLoader.js and trackers.js are also in `js/`. Sibling-flat require from `js/common/` — remember gh-823: "A lazy sibling-flat spec from js/common/ looks for js/x.js". So helpers can be in common/ too.

OK, different angle: which modules are "generic framework plumbing"? configLoader.js is THE config framework; trackers.js is THE tracker abstraction; config.js statuses. The reviewer's own framing: "worth checking why agentDocGenerator.js over-colects for JSRunner configs so the next generated agent doc doesn't inherit the noise."

Hmm — "for JSRunner configs". Maybe the intended fix: for JSRunner configs (which have no LM step and are pure plumbing consumers), only document customParams the action source itself reads (no transitive following)? But that contradicts gh-961 if a JSRunner action delegates to extracted helpers... gh-961 was about postTestAutomationResults (a Teamate agent).

Let me look at what docs exist for JSRunner agents and whether transitive collection ever mattered for them. JSRunner configs in root *.json: tc_differential_dispatcher.json, quota_park_probe.json... let me check which root configs are JSRunner and what their generated docs list.

# tc differential dispatcher

Scripted CI dispatcher for parked differential rerun requests (TC-failure attribution, gh-1329 follow-up). A pure local-execution job — no AI CLI, the run is the verdict.

When a validated guard TC fails and the automation leg's evidence cannot attribute the failure, the bug parks a differential rerun request in the TC maintenance ledger and carries the `tc_differential_pending` label (the SM rule queries it). This job — dispatched on the next SM tick, before any TC generator re-dispatches the bug — settles the request mechanically:

1. **Run** — checkout the request's recorded last-green build (`lastGreenSha`) in the target repo and run the single TC script. Nothing but the build varies.
2. **Route** — green on the old build → the change range caused the failure: the bug earns its bounce (moved to Ready For Development, evidence named in the comment). Red on the old build → the failure predates the change: the finding reopens as maintenance-debt sweep work. The bounce cap reached → owner escalation. A sibling-guard request never bounces its own bug.
3. **Resolve** — post the updated ledger marker (the consumed parked section disappears), post the route report, and clear the park label when nothing remains parked.

Unrunnable requests (no checkout target, no run command configured) stay parked fail-safe: one explanation comment on first attempt, quiet bumps afterwards, and the request remains visible in every ledger digest — an attribution stall is never silent.

## Parameters

- `tcRunCommand` (customParams) — the single-TC command template with a `{testPath}` placeholder (e.g. `pytest {testPath}`). Required for any request to run; without it all requests stay parked with an explanation comment.
- `workingDir` (customParams) — the target-repo checkout the TC scripts and git commands run in (default: project config `workingDir`).
- `maxReworkRounds` (customParams) — the earned-bounce cap before owner escalation (default: the triage engine's default).
- `parkLabel` (customParams) — the SM-matching park label (default `tc_differential_pending`). When overridden, the SM rule's JQL (`labels = tc_differential_pending`) must be overridden to match.

The corresponding SM rule lives in `sm.json` (`Parked differential rerun requests → scripted CI dispatch`): it matches bugs carrying the park label, stamps its own `sm_tc_differential_triggered` crash-recovery label, and runs before the bug TC-generator rule so a parked bug is settled before a fresh generation dispatch (the generator rule also skips `tc_differential_pending` bugs).

Unrunnable requests (no checkout target, no run command configured) stay parked fail-safe: one explanation comment on first attempt, quiet bumps afterwards, and the request remains visible in every ledger digest — an attribution stall is never silent.

The dispatcher validates the ledger-controlled inputs before any command is built: `lastGreenSha` must be a 7–64 char hex git SHA and `testPath` a plain repo-relative path (no shell metacharacters, no leading dash, no `..`). A rejected value routes to the `unavailable` fail-safe — nothing is executed and the request stays parked.

The deployment guard also applies here: with no `machineAuthor` allowlist configured (`params.jobParams.machineAuthor` or `config.machineAuthor`), the maintenance ledger parse fails closed and cannot see parked requests — the dispatcher bails (`unconfigured_parked`) without clearing the park label, and drops only its own `sm_tc_differential_triggered` lock so the next tick retries once the allowlist is fixed. When a dispatch finishes with nothing left parked, the job removes both the `tc_differential_pending` park label and its `sm_tc_differential_triggered` trigger label — the SM-side `addLabel` stays the in-flight crash guard, and a later park on the same bug dispatches again.

## Fail-closed allowlist can no longer strip the park label

`action` now resolves the deployment guard **before any ledger read or write** by reusing `bugBookkeeping.triageAllowlistWarning(params, config)`:

- `js/tcDifferentialDispatcher.js` — new `unconfiguredGuardResult()`: when the machine-author allowlist resolves empty (`js/common/bugBookkeeping.js` fail-closed behavior), the dispatcher logs the warning and bails with `{ success: true, action: 'unconfigured_parked', ticketKey }` — **the `tc_differential_pending` park label stays on**, no ledger marker, no comment, no shell execution. A genuinely parked request the fail-closed parse refused to read keeps its label: the dispatcher rule's JQL still matches it (no orphaning) and the generator rule's `tc_differential_pending` skip still applies (no unattributed re-dispatch) — the stall stays digest-visible, exactly the PR's fail-safe contract.
- The job's own `sm_tc_differential_triggered` lock **does** drop on this bail, so the next tick retries once the allowlist is configured — no permanent lock on an unconfigured fleet, no manual label surgery needed after the fix lands.
- The human doc (`docs/agents/tc_differential_dispatcher.md`) now documents this guard behavior alongside the existing deployment note.

Tests (`js/unit-tests/test_tcDifferentialDispatcher.js`, "unconfigured machineAuthor allowlist" suite):

- empty allowlist → `unconfigured_parked`, park label intact, zero comments/moves/shell calls;
- `config.machineAuthor` (the second resolution channel) satisfies the guard and dispatches normally;
- `jobParams.machineAuthor` (the factory setup channel) satisfies the guard (existing suite still green).

## Generated doc no longer inherits the plumbing channels

Root cause found in `js/agentDocGenerator.js`: `collectCustomParamsUsageFrom` followed local requires **transitively into the generic plumbing modules** — `configLoader.js` / `config.js` (the project-config system) and `common/trackers.js` (the tracker abstraction). # PR #1346 Rework — all 8 review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI `crap` ratchet (BLOCKING, thread 1)** — fixed. All 14 over-threshold functions refactored below the gate (behavior-preserving splits); verified locally against the released `crap-baseline` with the pinned `crap4js` + `nyc` pipeline: `0 regression(s), 0 new over threshold`.
- **`sm_tc_differential_triggered` never removed (BLOCKING, thread 2)** — fixed. The dispatcher now removes its trigger label alongside the park label when nothing remains parked (the `quotaParkProbe.liftPark` lifecycle); a second park on the same bug dispatches again (regression test included).
- **Fail-closed (empty `machineAuthor`) ledger read silently stripped the park label (BLOCKING, thread 3)** — fixed. `action` resolves `bugBookkeeping.triageAllowlistWarning(params, config)` before any read/write and bails with `action: 'unconfigured_parked'` — the park label stays, nothing is executed, and only the job's own trigger lock drops so the next tick self-heals once the allowlist is configured.
- **Ledger-controlled strings into shell commands (IMPORTANT, thread 4)** — fixed. `safeSha` (7–64 hex) + `safeTestPath` (no shell metacharacters / leading dash / `..`) validate before any command is built; rejections route to the existing `unavailable` fail-safe.
- **Unused `bugKey` param (suggestion, thread 5)** — fixed (`roleFieldsFromDescription` / `annotateWithRoles` are single-arg now; caller updated).
- **Generated doc lists 11 plumbing customParams (suggestion, thread 6)** — fixed at the root: `agentDocGenerator.js` no longer follows the generic plumbing modules (`configLoader.js` / `config.js` / `common/trackers.js`) when collecting customParams usage; all generated docs regenerated; the dispatcher doc lists exactly `tcRunCommand`, `workingDir`, `maxReworkRounds`, `parkLabel`.
- **`summaryOf`/`ticketFields` duplication (suggestion, thread 7)** — fixed (`issueTypeName` and `summaryOf` both go through the one `ticketFields` accessor).
- **Silent per-tick cap (suggestion, thread 8)** — fixed (`dispatchRequests` returns `deferred`; the report states `10-request-per-tick cap: N parked request(s) deferred to the next tick.`).

### CI failures

The failed check (`crap`) had **no machine-attributed owned-violations table** (`ci_violations.json`: 0 owned / 0 foreign / 8 unknown parse fragments — none carry a `path:line` in this PR's diff). The actionable content of the failure is the `CRAP Ratchet` block quoted in thread 1; every function it lists is in a file this PR changed and is now refactored under the threshold as above. The other 8 error lines in the raw log are unit-test log lines (`developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR` mock-rejection traces and a `Process completed with exit code 2.` fragment) with no attributable file — all of them come from the green unit suite itself (8174 passed locally).

## Approach

TDD per thread: failing tests first (`run_tcDifferentialDispatcher.json`: 12 new red tests across trigger-label lifecycle / allowlist guard / input validation / cap observability; `run_tcRoleStamp.json`: arity contract; `run_agentDocs.json` + `run_agentDocsCoverage.json`: plumbing-leak and dispatcher-doc pins; `run_stampTcRoles.json`: summary-fallback pin), then the minimal production change to green, then the CRAP refactor with all suites held green.

Verification: full-suite runs through **both** harnesses —
- `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` (canonical green gate) — green except one pre-existing sandbox-env failure (`sessionDelta UT-3 AC3` asserts the deterministic-fallback session dir; this shell exports a live `FA_SESSION_ROOT`/provider env from the running fa session — the same test passes with those env vars cleared and on CI's clean runner);
- the node coverage harness (CI's vehicle) — 8174 passed / 1 failed (the same env artifact);
- the quality gate replicated locally exactly as `.github/workflows/quality.yml` runs it (pinned `IstiN/crap4js@83ee6201`, `nyc`-instrumented tree, full-suite Istanbul coverage, released `crap-baseline.json`): ratchet exit 0; duplication ratchet exit 0.
- Agent docs regenerated (`node js/agentDocGenerator.js`, `node generate_agent_snapshots.js`) — the staleness gate stays satisfied.

## Files Modified

- `js/tcDifferentialDispatcher.js` — trigger-label lifecycle, allowlist guard (`unconfigured_parked`), sha/testPath validation, deferred-count reporting, CRAP splits.
- `js/common/tcRoleStamp.js` — `stampPlan` split (oracle election / sorted unmarked / planning), `roleFieldsFromDescription`/`annotateWithRoles` single-arg.
- `js/stampTcRoles.js` — accessor consolidation, `stampPhase`/`applyStampPlan`/`fieldsDescriptionOf` splits.
- `js/preCliStoryTestAutomationSetup.js` — one-arg `annotateWithRoles` call.
- `js/agentDocGenerator.js` — `PLUMBING_MODULES` skip in the transitive customParams collection.
- `js/unit-tests/test_tcDifferentialDispatcher.js` — new suites + hex-SHA fixtures + fixture CRAP splits.
- `js/unit-tests/test_tcRoleStamp.js`, `js/unit-tests/test_stampTcRoles.js`, `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — one-arg reads, scope-fallback pin, hex-SHA IT fixture.
- `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js`, `js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js` — config-loader mock carries `machineAuthor`; the node copy restructured into small merge helpers (ratchet).
- `js/unit-tests/test_agentDocs.js`, `js/unit-tests/test_agentDocsCoverage.js` — plumbing-leak + dispatcher-doc regression pins.
- `docs/agents/tc_differential_dispatcher.md` + all regenerated `docs/agents/generated/*.md` (56 files — plumbing noise removed repo-wide by the generator fix).
